A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study and contain 20 pages, including Appendices A–G. Text, equations, tables and rendered figures support reliable comparison despite layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original repeated-sampling experiments, importance-sampling comparisons, paraphrase analyses and held-out risk forecasts, including appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental outcomes in its main text and appendices, including harmful-response measurements, estimator comparisons and forecasting results.

M1.justification: The evaluated steering, model mixing/switching and proposal-selection pipeline is unchanged. New Section 10 sketches unevaluated adaptations for reasoning outputs and multi-turn interactions, including answer-only judging, a user simulator and trajectory-level importance weights.

E1.justification: The same STRONGREJECT queries, two 20-query misalignment datasets, paraphrases and steering-construction datasets are used. Reasoning and multi-turn scenarios appear only as future work.

E2.justification: Monte Carlo remains the comparator in the corresponding estimator evaluations. Figure 8 retains the same alternative steering-intensity proposals; no evaluated comparison method is added or removed.

E3.justification: Unsafe-query estimation retains 1,000 importance samples versus 10,000 Monte Carlo samples, proposal selection retains its 10% query subset, and forecasting retains the 30%/70% split. Judge thresholds and other reported experimental settings are unchanged.

E4.justification: Figure 6's paraphrase-sensitivity analysis loses its aggregate correlation and average-shift summaries. The per-query scatter comparisons, steering-strength ablation and appendix rewrite validation and case studies remain.

E5.justification: Uncertainty-reporting practices are unchanged, including the existing Clopper–Pearson 95% confidence-interval example. v2 adds no repeated-run counts, seed disclosures or significance tests.

E6.justification: Figure 6 removes correlations of 0.40 for Llama-3.1-8B, 0.25 for Qwen2.5-7B and 0.38 for Phi-4, plus average-shift values. Figure 7's observed-risk curves change slightly. Section 5 newly states that sycophancy is rarer than hallucination for both evaluated models; tabulated results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 10 adds reasoning/answer and multi-turn importance-weight formulations, a user-response distribution and trajectory-generation assumptions in Equations 7–9. Existing importance-sampling and extreme-value derivations, including Appendices E and F, remain unchanged apart from numbering.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central claims: sample-efficient harmful-output estimation, sensitivity to non-adversarial query rewrites and forecasting risk on unseen queries. The claimed 10–20-fold sampling advantage is unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 9 newly explains that small, leading-query datasets were selected to obtain measurable failure probabilities, leaving ordinary-user distributions untested. Section 10 explicitly identifies the non-reasoning, single-turn scope. Added discussion also connects judge costs and sycophancy rarity to the method's usefulness.

D1.justification: Appendices C, D and G retain the same judge prompts, steering implementation, data-construction details, paraphrasing prompt and generation parameters. The code-link target is unchanged, and the proposed extensions add no corresponding implementation or resource-use details.

R1.justification: The bibliography changes the Mazeika et al. entry from TDC2023 (LLM edition) to The Trojan Detection Challenge in the NeurIPS 2022 Competition Track, while Appendix D.1 still names TDC2023. Broader positioning relative to importance sampling and prior risk-forecasting work is unchanged.

P1.justification: Limitations are reorganized into named paragraphs, a Future Work section is inserted, and acknowledgments move after the Impact Statement. Local prose edits, correspondence details and conference information also change; the main narrative remains largely intact.

P2.justification: Figures 1, 6 and 7 receive visual revisions. Figure 6 changes colors, panel order and axes, explicitly displaying probabilities down to 10^-12; Figure 7 is redrawn and repositioned. Figure 2 and Table 1 move between columns, and the estimation pipeline gains a box.

improvement.justification: The expanded limitations clarify what the selected datasets establish and distinguish tested settings from proposed extensions, improving interpretation of deployment claims. The boxed pipeline also improves readability. These provide a modest net gain despite the loss of useful Figure 6 summaries; empirical support remains largely unchanged.
